newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Rubber prices firm at latest Colombo auctions.
newsitem.headline: Rubber prices firm at latest Colombo auctions.

text.p: Rubber prices were firm at Colombo auctions on strong demand by buyers worried over a shortage caused by drought, brokers and exporters said on Thursday.
"Superior grades met with very strong demand," said an exporter. "The market was almost unchanged but the tone is firmer. People are worried as very little rubber is available."

Best latex one-x, the purest grade, rose to 75.40 rupees per kg from 75.20 rupees on Tuesday, when the auction was last held. Number 1 rose to 74.75 rupees per kg from 74.50 rupees, while RSS 1 fell to 62 rupees from 62.50 rupees over the same period.
On offer were 169 tonnes of crepe, 50 tonnes of scrap crepe and 19 tonnes of sheet, brokers Forbes and Walker said.

"Prices moved up slightly due to lower quantities," said a Forbes and Walker broker. "We're expecting lower quantities next week due to the holidays for Friday's local government poll and to the effects of drought.
Many factories were running only half the day because of the lack of water, he said.
"There's not even enough water to wash the rubber. So the quality has come down," he said. ($1=Rs.57.62)
